content:
Sam L: hey all — first-week snag. trying to sign into 1Password CLI via Okta SSO for my dev laptop. i run `op signin redwood` and it opens the browser, i approve the push in Okta Verify, but the CLI then prints an error and exits. any known hoops?

Marie (IT): what exact error do you get? did you enroll Okta Verify on this device? also send me your okta username (email) via DM if you want — we can check your session. cc @Alex P for CLI quirks.

Sam L: pasting the output i see after approving the push:
```
> $ op signin redwood
Opening browser for authentication...
Browser returned error: 400 Bad Request
error_description: invalid_request: state_mismatch
Authentication failed: no active session
```
I'm on MacOS Ventura, using Chrome. Okta shows the push as accepted.

Alex P: hmm state_mismatch usually means the CLI and the browser flow didn't share the same state token (often cookies or a redirect got blocked). couple things to try: 1) temporarily disable any privacy/advert blocking in Chrome for the Okta url; 2) try an incognito window; 3) run the signin with `--raw` to get the token printed (v2 CLI): `op signin redwood --raw` then `eval $(op signin redwood --raw)` (wrap per your shell). also make sure you don't have another 1Password session in the browser.

Marie (IT): also check whether you have a corporate VPN on — sometimes the redirect goes to a different network and state gets lost. i can force-reset your Okta session if needed. Sam, can you try Alex's steps and paste any new output?

Sam L: tried incognito and turned off uBlock. got a different error now after approving:
```
Browser returned 'okta_redirect' but CLI timed out waiting for callback
Error: polling timed out (120s)
```
So it opens the okta redirect page fine but then the CLI waits and times out.

Alex P: ok that points to the CLI not receiving the callback. a quick workaround: use token-based signin: go to https://redwood.1password.com (or your 1Password web), sign in via browser SSO, open the 1Password extension or web vault, go to My Profile -> Developer -> Create CLI session token (if we have that flow enabled), copy the token into `eval $(op signin --raw <token>)`. if we don't have that enabled i'll ping IT to flip it.

Marie (IT): i just checked your Okta sessions, Sam — there were a couple stale ones. i cleared them and also reset your SSO callback sessions. try signing in again now. if it still times out i'll open a support ticket with 1Password.

DeployBot: Onboarding checklist update: Sam L completed "MFA enrollment" (Okta) at 2026-03-22 15:12 UTC.

Sam L: retried after the reset and it worked! ran `eval $(op signin redwood --raw)` and the CLI populated my env. thanks both.

Jess R: welcome to Redwood! glad it's sorted. ping if you need access to the infra vault — i'll add you to the dev team vault when you confirm your GitHub username. :party:
